date_note: Day the company announced the leak, per Daily SECU; the abnormal access ran from 4 to 6 November.
title: Welcome Payments says abnormal access to its merchant admin page leaked customer data
summary: Daily SECU reports that Welcome Payments announced a leak of payment-service users' data after abnormal access to its merchant admin page from 4 November 11:00 to 6 November 08:00. A notice on 24 November corrected the scale from 1,388 to 1,326 cases (건); a third notice on 26 November changed it to 1,327 cases, Daily SECU says. The company says card passwords and CVC were not leaked.
plain: Daily SECU reports Welcome Payments revised its leak figure again, to 1,327 cases. The company says card passwords and CVC codes were not leaked.
exec: A Korean payment gateway has revised the scale of its merchant-admin-page leak again, to 1,327 cases, Daily SECU reports.
action: Welcome Payments, per ZDNet Korea, urges users to be careful that the leaked data is not misused for voice phishing and smishing.

evidence.quote: 24일 웰컴페이먼츠는 지난 17일 오후 가맹점 관리자를 통해 개인 및 신용 정보가 유출됐으며 당시 1388건 정보가 유출됐다고 봤으나 다시 파악한 결과 1326건으로 줄었다고 밝혔다.
웰컴페이먼츠는 지난 11월 20일 개인정보 유출 사실을 공지한 데 이어 24일 오전 8시 35분 2차 안내를 통해 유출 규모를 기존 1,388건에서 1,326건으로 정정했다.
지난 11월 4일 오전 11시부터 6일 오전 8시까지 가맹점 관리자 페이지에 대한 비정상 접근이 발생했다.
웰컴페이먼츠는 26일 오전 8시 35분 공식 홈페이지에 개인정보 유출 관련 3차 수정 공지를 게시하고 기존 1,326건이었던 유출 규모를 1,327건으로 변경했다.

validation.note: Corroborated by two independent publishers, dailysecu.com (Daily SECU) and zdnet.co.kr (ZDNet Korea), each relaying the company's statement of the leak and the revision from 1,388 to 1,326 cases. They differ on timing: Daily SECU gives abnormal access 4 to 6 November; ZDNet Korea says the leak was via the merchant administrator on 'the 17th' (지난 17일 오후). The company's notices were not read.

review.note: action advice: said no action although the company urged caution against voice phishing and smishing (ZDNet Korea); now states it. Dates, 1,388 to 1,326, not-leaked data match Daily SECU and ZDNet. possible-duplicate flag with KIS/NHN KCP is false: different companies on one ZDNet article.
